> > Duality

Eh...I'd say it's about right, especially considering the versatility
of Vicissitude.

In terms of other vampires, the only baselines we have to compare this
with is Ira Rivers (Auspex) and Yseult (Melpominee).

- Ira spends a point to get his Auspex additional card ability and +1
intercept on political actions (the latter is half a point at most,
especially since unconditional +1 intercept is only a single point).
Then again, one could argue that this is mitigated by the fact that an
extremely large proportion of Auspex cards are Reactions (which limits
how useful his ability is).

- In Yseult's case, her Melpominee additional card ability seems to
balance out her restriction of not being able to block vampires bigger
than 4. It's kind of hard just how to judge this, but based on the
other Daughters of Cacophony (Sayshila excepted) and also Panders, it
does seem about right to say that her penalty is worth a point and her
special is worth a point. In addition, her special is less useful since
there are fewer Melpominee cards in existence. So in comparison to
Yseult, Duality seems appropriately costed.

In my personal opinion, being able to draw additional cards is most
valuable: #1. in combat, #2. with action modifiers, #3. with reactions,
#4. with actions. In combat, drawing additional cards often means the
difference of who goes to torpor and you can normally cycle cards
pretty efficiently, even more so with card drawing capability (see
Infernal Pursuit and Learjet). Drawing additional cards with action
modifiers helps you get the action through and is more valuable than
drawing additional cards with reactions because it is proactive rather
than reactive. And obviously, drawing additional cards when playing an
action is limited because it's only a single card you're playing at a
time.

Vicissitude is very much a combat discipline (with 16 combat cards out
of 25 total cards). There are also 5 action modifiers, and I've seen my
share of stealthy bleedy Tzimisce decks relying on Changeling + Plasmic
Form. So all in all, Duality's special seems to make him quite the
combat wombat, and also useful for cycling some stealth as well. I
think his ability serves him far better than Ira's or Yseult's
abilities help them, which is why I would say that he is appropriately
costed.

I agree that there has been a steady power creep the past few sets and
that typically the Malks/!Malks seem to get a lot of love, but I don't
think White Lily is an example of this (Louhi, Alicia, and Marie would
make better examples IMHO).

Maybe it's just me, but I actually think White Lily is subpar for what
you're paying for. Since she only has 7 discipline points, she's paying
an awful lot for her Black Hand and her special. And the lack of Auspex
really hurts her synergy with other members of her clan.

Compare to Teresita for example. Teresita has 7 points of disciplines
(just like White Lily). White Lily has Black Hand and a special.
Teresita has Black Hand, Seraph, and a minor special. White Lily is an
8 while Teresita is a 7.

White Lily's okay, but I really don't think she's all that. However I'm
certainly willing to entertain arguments that say otherwise.

Regarding the Gangrel/!Gangrel, I think they're pretty well off.
Protean is ridiculously good, they have access to great clan cards
(Gather, Bay and Howl, Leathery Hide). And though some of their large
caps aren't perfect, they generally have an excellent selection of
vampires (especially weenies and midcaps). Yeah, Xaviar sucks but
Enkidu and Una are quite good. Gangrel have plenty of sleazy DOM/PRO
(Stanislava, Ingrid, Iliana) and also some really annoying PRO/SER
(Mirembe and Nadima). And you can't go wrong with solid midcaps like
Horrock, Celeste, Janey, Harry, Darrell, and Sophia.

Um...just to make sure, are you saying that the !Tremere are getting
great stuff or crappy stuff?

Yeah, I guess if there's one thing that WotC & White Wolf are
consistant in, it's been giving the Tremere Antitribu the short end of
the stick. Even before the unceremonious genocide, they were constantly
being shat on by the Lasombra and Tzimisce (though surprisingly enough,
they garnered a significant amount of respect from the other Sabbat
clans). Even if it were thematic, one would hope that play balance &
fairness would take precedence. I mean, having to deal with Dauntain
Black Magician, Infamous Warlock, and Ayelea (who shows up in a
surprising number of Lasombra/Kiasyd decks) is bad enough, but Goratrix
Advanced was just adding insult to injury!

Thankfully, White Wolf has been nicer recently. We have Tupdogs to keep
Pugfar company (the ratio of Tremere:!Tremere slaves in Bloodlines was
disturbing). From KMW, Valerius Maior Advanced is kewl (though The Name
Forgotten is wallpaper). Gehenna brought the solid Ladislas Toth (and
the horribly crappy crappy CRAPPY Jacob the Glitch). Etc. Things have
been getting better, but the !Tremere are still a *long* way from
catching up with the other Sabbat clans, let alone the Camarilla and
Independents. (They're still down a clan card due to their absence in
Sabbat War and down an Advanced vampire since the Tremere poached
Goratrix in Black Hand).

In fact, I would argue that out of all the major (non-Bloodlines)
clans, the Tremere Antitribu are right near the bottom. Second-worst,
only a notch above the bottom-of-the-barrel Brujah Antitribu. (With the
addition of the Laibon, maybe the !Brujah and !Tremere can start a
"loser" club with the Osebo?). I'm really glad that both the !Brujah
and !Tremere are getting starters in 3rd Edition cause they seriously
need any boost they can get to make them at least marginally
competitive...

I'm not sure what the space-wedgie in playtest and the nerfing of Ian
refer to however. Care to enlighten me?

away all day. Etc. So play balance seems to be a likely culprit on why
Enkidu only has inferior Fortitude.

>Kevin Walsh wrote:
>> I'm kind of curious about why the Brujah Antitribu don't seem to do

>
>because everything they do can be done better with Brujah, with their
>access to dominate and second traditions. As for the crypt - yes, Sela
>is great, but so is Anvil. Amelia is good, but for only one extra pool,
>you can get Donal or Constanza with great specials, DOM and two votes.

Similarly, the Group 1/2 Brujah have some of the best access to
political clout in the game - Donal, Constanza, Rake, Volker, making
them much more versatile than just beats. The same versatility is
massively lacking in the !Brujah. They can get a small Priscus (group
4), or have two choices for Sela (group 2) so she can be a Bishop or
Archbishop, and Bishop isn't quite so crappy as Primogen, though doesn't
help as much for passing votes as a Prince. But this still isn't great.

The Brujah can use this to try to put together solid Archon vote-death
decks - and Archon is better than Templar, because of the blood hunt
immunity. Oh, and Anathema is better than, oh, the Sabbat don't have a
version of Anathema. And the Brujah have Carthage Remembered, and can
even use Oxford University to pass votes (making up for the lack of PRE
on key voters) and to drive the follow-up Parity Shift.

The !Brujah, on the other hand, have very solid combat in their mid-
caps. (Their weenies can be stolen and used by whoever, no problem.)
Which is great and all, except you don't want solid mid-cap combat -
it's not efficient enough, unless you can turn it into good multi-rush
(e.g. Tariq, Fatima etc.) or have good backup, like Anathema.

Number of !Brujah with Fortitude - 2. Richter, Miguel. Group 2, Group
3. Number of !Brujah with superior Fortitude. Zero. So block their
rushes, and untapping is much harder!

Similarly, 3 with Dom, none with DOM, 3 with Aus, none with AUS. Bleed
bounce is hard.

--
